title: Simple Sunday Honey Cake
subtitle: A tender, cozy cake sweetened with honey and perfect with tea or coffee

story.title: A Little Cake with a Big Hug
paragraphs: This is one of those dependable cakes I make when I want something sweet but simple. No fancy layers, no fussy frosting, just a soft crumb and warm honey flavor that makes the whole kitchen smell like comfort.
I call it Sunday Honey Cake because it is lovely for slow afternoons, catch-up chats, or a quiet treat after dinner. If you can stir and pour, you can make this one, dear. 🍯

ingredientGroups.title: For the Cake
items: ¾ cup plain yogurt or sour cream

steps.title: Prep the Pan and Oven
steps.body: Preheat your oven to 350°F. Grease and line an 8-inch square pan or 9-inch round cake pan with parchment paper so the cake lifts out easily.

steps.title: Mix the Dry Ingredients
steps.body: In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon. Set aside.

steps.title: Whisk the Wet Ingredients
steps.body: In a large bowl, whisk eggs, brown sugar, honey, oil, yogurt, and vanilla until smooth and creamy.

steps.title: Bring It All Together
steps.body: Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and gently fold just until no dry streaks remain. Do not overmix; a gentle hand keeps the cake tender.

steps.title: Bake Until Golden
steps.body: Pour batter into the prepared pan and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, or until the top is golden and a toothpick in the center comes out clean.

steps.title: Finish and Cool
steps.body: Let cake cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then move to a rack. If using glaze, stir honey, warm water, and cinnamon together and brush over the warm cake.

tips.title: Choose Mild Honey
tips.body: A mild floral honey gives sweetness without overpowering the cake. Strong buckwheat honey can taste a bit bold here.

tips.title: Keep It Moist
tips.body: Yogurt or sour cream gives this cake its soft texture. Full-fat versions make it extra tender.

tips.title: Perfect Pairing
tips.body: This cake is wonderful with black tea, coffee, or a little dollop of whipped cream if you are feeling fancy.

tips.title: Make Ahead Friendly
tips.body: It tastes even better the next day. Store covered at room temperature for up to 2 days, or refrigerate for 4 days.

variations.title: Orange Honey Cake
variations.body: Add 1 tablespoon orange zest to the batter for a bright citrus note.

variations.title: Walnut Crunch
variations.body: Fold in ½ cup chopped walnuts for a lovely little bite in each slice.

variations.title: Apple Honey Version
variations.body: Fold in 1 cup finely diced apple and add 5 extra minutes of bake time.

footer.heading: Sweet, Simple, and Full of Comfort
footer.text: When life feels busy, a simple honey cake and a warm cup can make everything feel softer.
